newsitem.title: KENYA: Rwanda says troops clash with Hutu militiamen.
newsitem.headline: Rwanda says troops clash with Hutu militiamen.

text.p: Rwanda's state news agency said on Tuesday five people including three civilians were killed in clashes between Rwandan troops and Hutu militiamen west of the capital.
The Rwandan News Agency, monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation, said clashes broke out on Monday in Runda village in Gitarama district, 12 km (seven miles) west of Kigali.

It quoted official sources in Gitarama as saying security forces fought with an armed group of former Rwandan Hutu troops and militiamen who were hiding in the area. It said a government soldier, a Hutu militiamen and three civilians were killed.
It said the three civilians were killed in cross-fire.
Human rights groups have accused Rwandan troops of at times killing civilians in reprisal for the killing of government soldiers and then saying the civilians were killed in cross-fire.
But they have also said attacks in western Rwanda have increased since the return of Hutu militiamen and troops among the more than 600,000 Rwandan Hutus came back to Rwanda late last year.
The refugees fled in 1994 in fear of reprisals for the killing of an estimated 800,000 Tutsis and Hutu moderates by Hutu troops, militiamen and mobs in a three-month genocide.
